clue.text: Well-read party that's considering writing?

parts.note: a gathering of keen readers who meet to discuss a chosen novel; 'party' suggests a celebration or a political group

explanation.surface: A literary gathering, or perhaps a political faction weighing up a written manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading group meets to talk over a novel its members have all read, so it is a sociable, literate gathering.

clue.text: Simple when written in pen

indicators.note: a word written in a pen sits inside it, so these letters go into the pen's brand name

parts.note: Bic is a well-known make of ballpoint pen
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something so easy it can be done in ink without fear of mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and elementary things are uncomplicated, which is what simple means.

clue.text: I will need one input — you will need two more

definitions.text: I will need one input — you will need two more

parts.words: I will need one input — you will need two more
parts.note: typing the letter I takes a single press on a keyboard; typing the word you takes three presses

explanation.surface: A boast that I contribute less effort than you do.
explanation.definitionFit: Each press of a key on a keyboard is one input, so a single letter needs one and a three-letter word needs three.

clue.text: China's rising rugby player, flier

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for China is read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: china is cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
a wing is a rugby position on the edge of the back line

explanation.surface: A Chinese rugby star on the up, flying down the touchline.
explanation.walkthrough: China = PAL is cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate. A wing plays out wide in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird also called the peewit is a flier, an example of something that flies.

clue.text: Their residents who sleep in are taught a lesson

definitions.text: Their residents who sleep in are taught a lesson

parts.words: Their residents who sleep in are taught a lesson
parts.note: pupils who board live at their place of education, so those sleeping there are taught lessons; 'sleep in' suggests oversleeping and being punished

explanation.surface: Lazy people who lie in bed too long get their comeuppance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep in' and 'taught a lesson' read as oversleeping and punishment; really they mean living on the premises and attending classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at residential academies live there during term, so the residents who sleep on site are taught lessons.

clue.text: Boy gets a thank you for composition

parts.note: a boy can be a son
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A child thanked for a piece of music he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of classical music in several movements is a type of composition.

clue.text: Twisted element of magic in a Tasmanian devil's character

indicators.note: twisted round means the run of letters found is read from right to left
an element of something is a part of it, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: A wicked streak in the nature of the snarling Australian marsupial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element of' finds CINATAS inside 'magic in a Tasmanian', and 'Twisted' reverses it. 'Tasmanian devil' looks like one phrase but Tasmanian is only hiding letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the nature of the devil means fiendish and wicked, like Lucifer himself.

clue.text: The aim's to be converted, having no church

definitions.note: the state of having no church, a noun sense of belonging to no faith

indicators.note: converting something changes its form, so these letters are rearranged; it also suits religious conversion

explanation.surface: A missionary's goal is conversion, which is awkward for someone with no church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' looks like religious conversion, the opposite of the answer, but it is the anagram signal for THE AIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief in God means belonging to no religion, so having no church describes it loosely.

clue.text: Commercial outfit beginning to export electronic letter opener

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
a dress is an outfit

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in email

explanation.surface: An advertised costume, or an email-opening gadget for export.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter opener' suggests a paperknife; here it is the person who opens the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter is sent to is the one who opens it, so the recipient is the letter opener.

clue.text: Be suspended and delay the sack?

definitions.meaning: to remain hanging aloft, not falling
the sack is slang for bed, so to delay it is to not go to bed

explanation.surface: An employee on suspension trying to put off being fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining aloft is one sense; delaying bedtime late at night is the other, since sack is slang for bed.

clue.text: Chat with date, excited to get engaged?

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A chat and a date are so thrilling that a couple decide to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a relationship or about to marry is committed, a sense of engaged.

clue.text: Made a bob on getting to meet the Queen?

definitions.text: Made a bob on getting to meet the Queen?

parts.words: Made a bob on getting to meet the Queen?
parts.note: a bob is a quick bend of the knee given as a greeting to royalty; 'made a bob' suggests earning a shilling

explanation.surface: Someone earned a shilling by meeting the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was British slang for a shilling, so 'made a bob' hints at earning money; really it is a respectful bend of the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: Women traditionally dip with bent knees when presented to the monarch, a polite bob.

clue.text: Order mixer only to be added?

parts.note: a bar order for just a mixer means leave out the frozen cubes, split as two words saying no frozen water

explanation.surface: A customer at the bar asks for just a mixer in their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, NOT ICE is the instruction that only the mixer goes in, leaving the cubes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal announcement telling people what to do, such as a notice to quit, is an order.

clue.text: Vehicle sabotaged to go bang

indicators.note: something sabotaged is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A car tampered with so that it will explode.
explanation.definitionFit: A long sled for sliding down snowy slopes is a vehicle, a means of transport.

clue.text: Flying ace doubly hot, in biting pain

indicators.note: flying around wildly, so these letters scatter and rearrange
doubly means the word hot is taken twice

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot in a hot cockpit suffering a fierce pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' gives HOTHOT; 'Flying' shuffles that with ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache in a molar is a pain felt where you bite, so biting pain is a playful description.

clue.text: Vast area of 100 miles covered by Ordnance Survey twice

indicators.note: each letter is followed, or covered, by the map-makers' initials

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
OS is Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency
twice means the Ordnance Survey letters appear a second time

explanation.surface: A huge tract of land a hundred miles across, mapped twice by Britain's surveyors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is Britain's official map-maker; its initials follow both C and M.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole universe is the vastest area there is, a poetic description of all space.

clue.text: Support for someone unfortunately getting carried away

definitions.text: Support for someone unfortunately getting carried away

parts.words: Support for someone unfortunately getting carried away
parts.note: an injured person is carried off on a frame of canvas between poles; 'carried away' usually means overexcited

explanation.surface: Backing for a friend who has got rather too excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried away' reads as losing self-control; here it is literal, an injured player borne off the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas litter held by two bearers supports a casualty while they are carried off.

clue.text: Acclimatise in Japan maybe

definitions.meaning: to get used to new surroundings, find one's bearings
Japan is an example of a country of the East, the lands of Asia

explanation.surface: Getting used to life while living in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: To find one's bearings means to adjust; the East, including Japan, is called by the old name for eastern lands.

clue.text: Fashionable company meets occasionally to deliver these?

definitions.text: Fashionable company meets occasionally to deliver these?

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

indicators.note: occasionally means taking letters at intervals, every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A trendy firm whose board meets now and then to keep the salaries flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes the first, third and fifth letters of 'meets'. The whole clue also defines: a smart firm pays out wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A company delivers earnings to its staff in the form of salaries and wages.

clue.text: News items with hospital being scrapped I'd put in

indicators.note: put in means the letters go inside what remains
something scrapped is thrown away, so this letter is removed

parts.note: things are items
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital closure making headlines, with a reporter adding their piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being scrapped' drops the hospital letter from the word for items, and 'put in' places the reporter's I'D inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old-fashioned word for news, as in 'glad tidings'.

clue.text: Pipes in sight carrying whiskey explode

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the letter goes within the word for sight

parts.note: to see is to sight something
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to explode with anger is to rage

explanation.surface: Drinkers smoking pipes in view, with a bottle of whiskey, flying into a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: The network of drains carrying waste is a system of pipes.

clue.text: Western delta is wild — around November it rarely dries out

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the next one
wild means out of control, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A river delta in the west that turns wild and stays damp after November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges DELTA, and 'around' wraps those letters round N. 'Is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshes and swamps are waterlogged land that seldom dry out, a fair description.

clue.text: Cut two journalists

parts.note: the two journalists: a hack is a journalist
the second journalist: ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A pair of reporters lose their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopped roughly with a blade is one sense of cut.

clue.text: Chilli sauce, perhaps it's stolen

definitions.meaning: spicy food, with chilli sauce as an example of something fiery
hot is slang for stolen, and stuff means things, so the phrase is stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone has made off with the chilli sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiery food is spicy, while stolen goods are called hot; the phrase covers both senses.

clue.text: Beast could be intimate without resistance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word for intimate

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend
R is the symbol for resistance in physics

explanation.surface: A brute who might become close if only he stopped resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon or a cruel person is a beast, a wicked creature.

clue.text: Ban-the-bombers holding missiles back ring military man?

indicators.note: holding means the letters are enclosed by the campaigners' initials

parts.note: CND is the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, the British ban-the-bomb movement

indicators.note: back means the word for missiles is read in reverse

parts.note: ammo, ammunition, is missiles
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: Peace protesters clutching weapons as they ring a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Ban-the-bombers are Britain's Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament; 'holding' wraps their initials round the missiles turned 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier trained for raids is an example of a military man.

clue.text: Some characters on board splash or escape to the beach

indicators.note: some of the letters written here contain the answer; characters are letters

explanation.surface: Passengers on a ship splash about or flee to the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Going onto land from the sea means heading to the beach, onto the shore.

clue.text: Express found among European ship's papers

indicators.note: found among means placed between the letters for the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to express is to say

explanation.surface: Express mail discovered among a European vessel's documents.
explanation.definitionFit: School or academic compositions are called papers, short written pieces.

clue.text: Turning left maybe, went by bike reportedly?

parts.note: left is an example of a side

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than read, so the past tense of ride gives its sound-alike

parts.note: rode means went by bike

explanation.surface: Someone turns left, perhaps, on their bicycle trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor street branching off a main one is a turning, as in 'take the next turning'.
